description: LL-37 is a 37-amino-acid cationic amphipathic peptide derived from the human cathelicidin precursor (CAMP). It is the reference human host-defence peptide and is used in membrane-interaction, antimicrobial-susceptibility and innate-immunity research, where its activity depends strongly on peptide concentration, ionic strength and membrane composition.

faq.question: What is LL-37?
faq.answer: LL-37 is a 37-amino-acid human cathelicidin-derived host-defence peptide (CAS 154947-66-7), supplied as a laboratory reference peptide.

faq.question: Is the sequence and precursor documented?
faq.answer: Yes — the page states the full sequence and its position within the human cathelicidin precursor (UniProt P49913). Identity is verified by mass spectrometry per batch.

faq.question: Why does LL-37 activity vary between experiments?
faq.answer: Because host-defence peptide activity is sensitive to salt concentration, pH, serum content and membrane composition. We therefore publish no fixed potency figure — the relevant analytical data are the purity and identity results on the COA.

faq.question: What does a kit contain?
faq.answer: 10 mg × 10 vials per kit (price-list code 375), lyophilized, with a batch-specific COA.
